claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian and biblical scholar born around 185 CE in Alexandria and died around 254 CE in Tyre.

He taught at the Catechetical School of Alexandria and succeeded Clement as its head under the authority of Bishop Demetrius, later founding a school in Caesarea and being ordained a priest by the bishops of Caesarea and Jerusalem.
The homilies on Judges were delivered sometime between 238 CE and 248 CE.
They were composed as a series of nine sermons that expound on Judges 2‑7 and use Origen’s allegorical method to draw spiritual meaning for Christian believers.
Origen addresses the sermons to a Christian audience, calling them to participate in a loving relationship with Christ through Scripture.
The work was intended to teach the faithful how Scripture can lead to knowledge of Christ, promote virtue, and demonstrate that ultimate victory belongs to God alone.
